scientific_hypothesis: A 24-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 stack with individual layer thicknesses optimized from quarter-wave starting values at 550 nm can simultaneously achieve high reflectance in 400-700 nm and high transmittance in 1530-1565 nm without requiring chirped or aperiodic layer sequences.
expected_advantages: Simple periodic topology is easier to manufacture than chirped or aperiodic designs
Quarter-wave starting point provides good initial performance, reducing optimization iterations needed
24 layers leaves manufacturing margin within the 30-layer constraint
HfO2 and SiO2 are standard, well-characterized coating materials with low absorption in both bands
known_risks: Uncertain: Exact refractive index values for hfo2 and sio2 across 400-1565 nm - would need to verify from material_catalog datasets
Uncertain: Whether HfO2 has significant absorption below 450 nm that would reduce visible reflectance - would need to check extinction coefficient data
Uncertain: Whether 12 pairs provides sufficient visible reflectance (>90%) or if more pairs would be needed - may require increasing to 14-15 pairs
Uncertain: Incidence angle not specified in request; assuming normal incidence (0°) but satellite applications may have off-axis rays - angular sensitivity not tested in this route
Uncertain: Polarization state not specified; assuming unpolarized or testing both TE/TM - polarization splitting at oblique angles not addressed

Trade-off given up: Not exploring chirped or aperiodic layer sequences that might provide sharper band edges; not exploring alternative center wavelengths; not exploring different starting layer (SiO2-first vs HfO2-first)
expected_observations: best_target_score should increase across optimization rounds as layer thicknesses converge toward optimal values
tightest_margin should remain non-negative across rounds, indicating physically valid candidates throughout
valid_candidates count should remain high (not dropping to zero), indicating the search space is well-bounded
If hypothesis is correct: final design shows reflectance >85% in 400-700 nm band AND transmittance >90% in 1530-1565 nm band
If hypothesis is incorrect: best_target_score plateaus at low value indicating fundamental topology limitation, or one band performance degrades to improve the other
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the thickness optimization axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best thickness set
If valid_candidates drops below 5 for two consecutive rounds, relax thickness bounds by 20% and continue; if still failing after relaxation, stop and flag topology may need revision
If tightest_margin falls below -0.1 for any candidate, that candidate is invalid but continue searching; if all candidates invalid for two rounds, stop and report infeasible starting bounds
